newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares close firmer on moderate volume.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares close firmer on moderate volume.

text.p: * NZ shares close firmer as selected leaders prosper
* Lion, Carter and FCL Paper gains offset Telecom's fall
* Cultus streaks ahead on new oil estimates
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index +6.46 at 2,339.33

New Zealand shares closed firmer on Thursday as selected leading stocks made strong gains on moderate volumes.
"We've seen various good buying in the market again, although it is a bit quieter today," said Tim Koller at Merrill Lynch. The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 6.46 points stronger at 2,339.33.

Telecom's six cent fall to NZ$6.94 was more than offset by the good performances of Lion Nathan, which rose ten cents to $3.81, Fletcher Paper, up five at $3.28, and Carter Holt Harvey, up four to $3.40.

Brokers said market rumours that Australian softdrink bottler Cadbury Schweppes was about to buy Lion's Pepsi-Cola division were bUOying the stock. Lion has said the deal, while not off the agenda, is still a long time away from happening.
Gains in foresters Carter Holt and FCL Paper were on the back of the view that the pulp and paper cycle had bottomed, brokers said, although Koller noted the perception was not universal.
"Some people view the short-term upside (in the pulp and paper cycle) as being minimal -- maybe a double-dip scenario," he said.
Several smaller stocks enjoyed hefty rises on the day, but none was able to beat Cultus Petroleum's 40 cent gain to an all-time high of NZ$4.30.
The Australasian oil and gas exploration company said new estimates showed between 617 million and 2.665 billion barrels of oil were in place in its Cornea field, offshore Western Australia.
-- Matthew Brockett, Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 473-3736
